newsitem.title: USA: PC-stocks continue to surge, several factors cited.
newsitem.headline: PC-stocks continue to surge, several factors cited.

text.p: PC stocks surged again to new heights, with several factors cited as fueling Wednesday's climb, but some analysts warned that there is an element of "irrational exuberance" in the recent jump in PC stocks.

Analysts said that expected price cuts from chip giant Intel Corp, which started to tell computer makers about its coming price cuts, will fuel more demand for PCs, as PC makers cut prices. Intel's price cuts are expected July 28.
Some analysts also pointed to coming market research data on PC growth in the second quarter, which will be officially published Monday by two major market research firms.

Analysts said the data -- to be released by both market research firms Dataquest Inc and International Data Corp -- will show further market share gains by the leaders, especially Dell Computer Corp and Compaq Computer Corp, and continued strength from International Business Machines Corp and Gateway 2000 Inc.
"This is not a surprise," said one technology trader. "Dell, Gateway and Compaq, they are eating everyone's lunch."
A third factor is the expectation that earnings on Thursday from direct PC marketer Gateway 2000 may not be as disappointing as previously anticipated.

"They have already pre-announced and said 'we will be a bit weak'," said Lou Mazzucchelli, a Gerard, Klauer & Mattison analyst. "Unless Gateway falls off the desk, any positive signals by Gateway will be magnified by Dell. I believe the direct model will continue to show gains."

All the shares of the leading PC makers soared to new 52-week highs Wednesday. Compaq shares soared 7-7/16 to a new high of 138-15/16, Dell Computer climbed four to 164, also a new high, and Gateway 2000 jumped three to 44-3/4, a new high, on a post-split basis. IBM tacked on 2-1/8 to close at 105-1/8, after falling back from a new high of 107, post split.

"The preliminary numbers may show much better market share growth," said Daniel Ries, a Nomura Securities analyst, compared to Wall Street's previous expectations for the second quarter PC data. "Some of those numbers may be leaking out."

Kimball Brown, a PC analyst at Dataquest Inc in San Jose, Calif., said that the PC market share data will not be available to Dataquest clients until Friday. "It's quite positive though," he said, but he would not comment further.
On average, Compaq, Dell and Gateway are up about 8-10 percent since Friday. IBM lags and is up only 0.72 percent.
This compares to a 1.34 percent gain in the NASDAQ Composite since Friday and a 2.34 percent gain in the S&P 500.
Analysts said that these leading technology stocks are just now starting to catch up to the rest of the market, since many technology stocks lagged the market's huge rally so far.
"We are in unchartered territory for some of these companies," said Mazzucchelli. Dell is currently trading at a price/earnings ratio of about 32 times fiscal 1998 estimates.
"There is an element of 'irrational exuberance' in some of the PC stocks," he added, referring to broad market comments made in December by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
